'''Jo Emily Handelsman''' (born March 19, 1959) is the Director of the Wisconsin Institute for Discovery at [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.wisc.edu/jo-handelsman-named-director-of-wisconsin-institute-for-discovery/|title=Jo Handelsman named director of Wisconsin Institute for Discovery|website=news.wisc.edu|access-date=2016-12-01|author=Natasha Kassulke|date=November 29, 2016}}</ref> She is also a Vilas Research Professor and a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] Professor.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://wid.wisc.edu/people/jo-handelsman/|title=Jo Handelsman|date=2018-05-01|website=Wisconsin Institute for Discovery|language=en-US|access-date=29 January 2026}}</ref> Handelsman was appointed by President Barack Obama as the Associate Director for Science at the White House [[Office of Science and Technology Policy]], where she served for three years until January 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/node/290076|title=Jo Handelsman|website=The White House|language=en|access-date=2020-03-08}}</ref> She has been editor-in-chief of the academic journal ''[[DNA and Cell Biology]]'' and author of books on [[Scientific teaching|scientific education]], most notably ''Scientific Teaching''.<ref name="yale profile">{{cite web|url=http://bbs.yale.edu/people/jo_handelsman-2.profile|title=Jo Handelsman, PhD Profile|publisher=Yale School of Medicine|accessdate=10 September 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100622110010/http://bbs.yale.edu/people/jo_handelsman-2.profile|archive-date=22 June 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="hhmi">{{cite web|url=http://www.hhmi.org/grants/professors/handelsman_bio.html|title=Jo Handelsman, Ph.D.|publisher=Howard Hughes Medical Institute|accessdate=10 September 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Brumfiel |first1=G. |last2=Tollefson |first2=J. |last3=Hand |first3=E. |last4=Baker |first4=M. |last5=Cyranoski |first5=D. |last6=Shen |first6=H. |last7=Van Noorden |first7=R. |last8=Nosengo |first8=N. |last9=Butler |first9=D.

==Education==
Handelsman was born on March 19, 1959, in [[New York City]]. She earned her [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[agronomy]] from [[Cornell University]] in 1979 and her Ph.D. in [[molecular biology]] from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in 1984.<ref name="CV">{{cite web|url=http://www.unh.edu/news/docs/handelsmancv.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|publisher=The University of New Hampshire|accessdate=10 September 2010}}</ref>

==Career==
Handelsman secured a faculty position in plant pathology at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in 1985. She remained at Wisconsin until 2009, and then took a position at the Yale University Department of Molecular, Cellular and Developmental Biology in 2010.<ref name="yale profile"/><ref name="hhmi"/><ref name="Gellman">{{cite web|url=http://www.yaledailynews.com/news/2010/feb/01/prof-to-push-diversity/|title=Prof. to push diversity|last=Gellman|first=Lindsay|date=February 1, 2010|publisher=Yale Daily News|accessdate=10 September 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120920195824/http://www.yaledailynews.com/news/2010/feb/01/prof-to-push-diversity/|archive-date=20 September 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her research involves the study of [[microorganism]]s present in soil and insect [[gut (anatomy)|gut]].<ref name="yale profile"/> She is responsible for coining the term [[metagenomics]]<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Handelsman | first1 = J. | last2 = Rondon | first2 = M. R. | last3 = Brady | first3 = S. F. | last4 = Clardy | first4 = J. | last5 = Goodman | first5 = R. M. | title = Molecular biological access to the chemistry of unknown soil microbes: A new frontier for natural products | journal = Chemistry & Biology | volume = 5 | issue = 10 | pages = R245–R249 | year = 1998 | doi = 10.1016/S1074-5521(98)90108-9 | pmid=9818143| doi-access = free }}</ref> and is particularly known for her work in pioneering the use of functional metagenomics to study antibiotic resistance.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1111/j.1462-2920.2004.00664.x| pmid = 15305923| title = Uncultured soil bacteria are a reservoir of new antibiotic resistance genes| journal = Environmental Microbiology| volume = 6| issue = 9| pages = 981–9| year = 2004| last1 = Riesenfeld | first1 = C. S. | last2 = Goodman | first2 = R. M. | last3 = Handelsman | first3 = J. | bibcode = 2004EnvMi...6..981R| s2cid = 10738923}}</ref> She has published books and held workshops on scientific teaching, for which she is recognized nationally.<ref name="hhmi"/>

She is a researcher and advocate of women in science issues. One of Handelsman's seminal studies found that the gender of a name on a science resume affected a professor's inclination to hire, mentor, and pay applicants for a lab position.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Moss-Racusin|first1=Corinne|display-authors=etal|title=Science faculty's subtle gender biases favor male students|journal=Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A.|date=2012|volume=109|issue=41|pages=16474–9|doi=10.1073/pnas.1211286109|pmc=3478626|bibcode=2012PNAS..10916474M|pmid=22988126|doi-access=free}}</ref> She was co-director of the Women in Science and Engineering Leadership Institute<ref name="newswise">{{cite web|url=http://www.newswise.com/articles/view/513809/|title=Despite Gains, Women Still Face Bias in Science Careers|date=2005-08-15|publisher=Newswise, Inc|accessdate=17 January 2011}}</ref><ref name="WISELI">{{cite web|url=http://wiseli.engr.wisc.edu/people/handelsman.php|title=WISELI|publisher=Board of Regents of the University of Wisconsin System|accessdate=17 January 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720114339/http://wiseli.engr.wisc.edu/people/handelsman.php|archive-date=20 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was the first president of the Rosalind Franklin Society.<ref name="yale profile"/><ref name="rfs">{{cite web|url=http://www.rosalindfranklinsociety.org/about/board-officers|title=Rosalind Franklin Society|publisher=Rosalind Franklin Society|accessdate=1 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190403230610/http://www.rosalindfranklinsociety.org/about/board-officers|archive-date=3 April 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> She is also the co-author of six books on the topic of teaching and education.<ref name=":0" /> 
==Honors and awards==
In 2008, Handelsman received the [[Alice C. Evans Award]] from the [[American Society for Microbiology]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=ASM Alice C. Evans Award for Advancement of Women |url=https://asm.org/academy/asm-alice-c-evans-award-for-advancement-of-women |access-date=2026-10-09 |website=ASM |language=en}}</ref> and in 2011 was awarded the [[Presidential Award for Excellence in Science, Mathematics, and Engineering Mentoring|Presidential Award for Excellence in Science, Mathematics and Engineering Mentoring]] from the [[National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-18 |title=Presidential Awards for Excellence in Science, Mathematics and Engineering Mentoring {{!}} NSF - U.S. National Science Foundation |url=https://www.nsf.gov/honorary-awards/paesmem |access-date=2026-10-09 |website=www.nsf.gov |language=en}}</ref>  In 2015, she gave the third annual [[Patrusky Lecture]] from the [[Council for the Advancement of Science Writing]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Patrusky Lectures |url=https://casw.org/events/the-patrusky-lectures/ |access-date=2026-10-09 |website=CASW}}</ref> She was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] as a Fellow in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://members.amacad.org/content/members/newFellows.aspx|title=2019 Fellows and International Honorary Members with their affiliations at the time of election|website=members.amacad.org|url-status=dead|access-date=2020-03-08|archive-date=2020-03-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302174101/https://members.amacad.org/content/members/newFellows.aspx}}</ref> In 2020, she was awarded the Viktor Hamburger Outstanding Educator Prize from the [[Society for Developmental Biology]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Society for Developmental Biology {{!}} Viktor Hamburger Outstanding Educator Prize |url=https://www.sdbonline.org/hamburger_prize |access-date=2026-10-09 |website=www.sdbonline.org}}</ref>  In 2023, she was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2023-nas-election.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230502194908/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2023-nas-election.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=May 2, 2023 | title=2023 NAS Election }}</ref>
